messages:
maya: quick question about the prompt/prefix cache contract — should we expose cache-hit metadata in response headers or in the response body? also how do we signal hits for streaming responses?

devin: my vote is headers for non-streaming so we don't change body shape. for streaming we can either add a small control chunk at the start or mirror the header as the first JSON control frame. headers are easiest for proxies/observability.

alex-k: note: some clients (browsers/ EventSource) don't expose all headers when streaming. pragmatic approach = headers + a tiny control frame for streams. e.g.:

```
:meta {"cache_hit": true, "cache_key_version": "v2", "cache_status": "hit"}
<stream tokens>...
```

samir: compatibility concern — older clients read `cached` boolean in the body. If we only add headers, SDKs might break. can we keep body fallback?

devin: agree we should keep a body fallback during rollout. proposal: add header `x-rw-prompt-cache: hit|miss|stale` + `x-rw-prompt-cache-version: v1|v2`. For non-streaming responses keep a `cached` boolean in the JSON for a transition period. For streaming, emit the control frame as alex suggested.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-15T08:12Z for service=prefix-cache-service succeeded :white_check_mark:

maya: names for headers i propose: `x-rw-prompt-cache`, `x-rw-prompt-cache-version`, `x-rw-prompt-cache-reason` (reason values like `ttl`, `prefix_mismatch`, `kv_miss`)

cheng: enum values should be stable: `hit`, `miss`, `bypass`, `partial`. please make reason small set too.

zara: invalidation mechanics: publish to `cache-invalidate-prefix` topic with payload `{key, version, reason}`. consumers (dedicated/private) can subscribe. add an allowlist for high-frequency keys.

samir: also API-level option: `cache_policy` query param with values `prefer_cache|bypass|no_cache` to let callers override. prefer not to abuse standard Cache-Control since proxies treat differently.

devin: prefer a dedicated query param or header `x-rw-cache-policy`. keep it small. rollout strategy: default to current behavior (body `cached`) and opt-in to header+control-frame via `x-rw-cache-opt-in: v2`. after 3 weeks flip default and keep `cached` body until 1 month post-flip.

maya: concrete action items so we don't lose this: 1) PR to add headers + body fallback (owner: @devin) 2) PR for streaming control-chunk format (owner: @alex-k) 3) infra topic + invalidation doc + consumer guide (owner: @zara) 4) SDK/client shim + e2e tests for compatibility (owner: @cheng) 5) add enum and reason docs in API contract (owner: @samir). I'll open the RFC with these as checklist.

alex-k: I'll draft example for streaming control chunk format:

```
:meta {"x-rw-prompt-cache":"hit","version":"v2","partial":false}
{"role":"assistant","delta":"Hello"}
{"role":"assistant","delta":" world"}
```

devin: sgtm. for header content let's standardize value set: `hit|miss|stale|partial`. `x-rw-prompt-cache-reason` optional with short tokens.

maya: can we add CI e2e that asserts both header present and body `cached` fallback for non-streaming, and control-chunk present for streaming? @cheng please add to test matrix.

cheng: yep — will add node-fetch + xhr + python clients to CI. will include a test for `x-rw-cache-opt-in` behavior.

maya: timeline: RFC today, PRs this week, opt-in canary next week. tagging for follow-up in RFC: @devex for SDK visibility, @security for header leakage concerns.

samir: one last thought: we should include `cache_key_version` in logs/traces to make invalidations debuggable.

maya: good call. add `x-rw-prompt-cache-version` to response header and include in traces. thanks everyone :tada:
